encounters.cc: Increasing lethargy and poor feeding with yellowing of skin first noticed after discharge

lines: Increasing lethargy and poor feeding with yellowing of skin first noticed after discharge

The patient is a former 39-week newborn with VACTERL association who has undergone recent interventions for tracheoesophageal fistula with esophageal atresia, coarctation of the aorta, and posterior urethral valves, and who returns to the emergency department approximately one month after discharge with symptoms of progressive jaundice.
He was born at 39 weeks via spontaneous vaginal delivery after an uncomplicated pregnancy.
No resuscitation was required, and Apgar scores were 8 and 9 at 1 and 5 minutes.
The infant was discharged home at 48 hours of life.
Parents report that mild yellowing of the skin was first noticed within the first 24 hours after birth and has progressively worsened.
Over the past two days, the infant has become more difficult to wake for feeds, and when he does latch, he often sucks weakly and quickly falls asleep.
They also describe a new intermittent high-pitched cry and occasional arching of the back.
The infant had previously received phototherapy at a community clinic, but bilirubin levels continued to rise.
